design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (pap_supply_replenishment, Self-Pay Supply Subscription world). frozen_time 2026-10-14 11:30:00 EDT.

0. DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 4, 4]}; every computation carries four factors. Occupied by task 0: resupply_ext_refill_request_items, resupply_ext_covered_filter_units, resupply_ext_wrong_cushion_reship_units, resupply_ext_continued_use_proof_date and their tools (refill request, covered line, no-charge replacement, continued-use proof). This task claims the remaining, disjoint space: resupply_ext_rush_shipping_charge (root, pay_expedited_shipping_41dc5e4a, owner=user), resupply_ext_standing_order_charge (book_subscription_line_cd282959), resupply_ext_ground_charge_catch_up (book_ground_shipping_charge_38ca3aab) and resupply_ext_recorded_style_from_use (update_mask_style_bfa4256b). Together the two tasks cover all eight extended policies; nothing is reserved. Route-around notes: (a) holdings carry no numeric field, so the recorded-style problem's scored value is the mask_style the enrollment records, computed from the enrollment's own lines; (b) the base confirmation_fresh gate binds every shipped line to a refill confirmation, although the base rule itself exempts automatic shipments, so the standing-order policy declares an overwrite of that sentence that keeps the schedule's refill lead-day window for every line that rests on a refill confirmation and exempts the automatic-shipment standing-order line (whether a coverage-billed line must rest on a request still follows the base rule; no-charge reships are not held to the window); (c) the base self-pay discount clause and the two shipping-fee clauses are overwritten by declared sentences (owner discount; ground catch-up fee, floor and late share; rush fee, credit, share and softener).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Gerald Fenwick pays for his supplies himself on an automatic monthly subscription and only asks for this month's box to be rushed before a work trip, paying the rush fee. The rush policy fixes the charge only after (i) the standing-order cushion line due stands booked on today's shipment and (ii) the newest earlier ground shipment carries the ground charge it owes; the standing-order line in turn is booked only after the recorded mask style matches what his own lines show. In the records: his cushion supply ran out 2026-10-13 with no line today; the 2026-09-25 add-on box went out by ground with no shipping charge; and the enrollment still records full_face while his branch purchases since August are nasal pillows (plus one nasal cushion). The agent has to find each of these from the records, compute four values (style, catch-up charge, line amount, rush charge) and hand Gerald the payment step.

2. POLICIES CLAIMED. base_policy_refs: style -> [resupply_item_compatibility, resupply_order_continuity] (subject resupply_preference_update); standing line -> the six base policies on resupply_item_shipped; ground catch-up and rush -> [resupply_shipping]. Triggers: rush on_request; the other three state_due (a due standing-order cycle, an unpaid ground charge and a stale style are owed whatever he called about). Overwrites: standing line -> resupply_refill_confirmation's confirmation_fresh sentence and resupply_self_pay_pricing's subscription-discount clause; ground catch-up -> resupply_shipping's ground-fee sentence; rush -> resupply_shipping's expedited-fee sentence; style -> [].

3. FACTOR CARD (figures from the replay harness, identical to check_compute).
 resupply_ext_recorded_style_from_use (result nasal_pillows; all baselines full_face):
  evidence_lines [method]: branch-collected self-pay lines exist (2026-08-21 A7034 and A7033 x2, 2026-09-18 A7033 x2, 2026-10-03 A7032 x1) -> they count, standing-order lines do not; baseline (every line counts) adds the standing A7031 lines of 2026-07-20, 08-17, 09-14, A7031 wins on lines -> full_face.
  look_back_span [parameter]: 4 branch lines in 6 months -> 3 months; baseline 1 month keeps only 09-18 A7033 and 10-03 A7032, a tie the newer nasal cushion wins with 1 line < 2 -> full_face.
  candidate_pick [method]: two cushion items counted -> most lines (A7033, 2 lines) is the candidate; baseline (newest line's item) picks A7032 with 1 line -> full_face. Near-miss: the newest branch line is a nasal cushion.
  switch_threshold [parameter]: the nasal interface A7034 was collected within the span -> 2 lines; baseline 4 lines -> full_face.
 resupply_ext_ground_charge_catch_up (result 2.97; all baselines 0):
  compared_value [method]: the 2026-09-25 box has no cushion or mask line -> the amount charged 78.20 is compared; baseline list value 92.00 >= 85 -> 0.
  free_ship_floor [parameter]: subscription opened 2025-03-03, 19 months -> 85.00; baseline 75.00 (78.20 >= 75) -> 0.
  late_booking_share [parameter]: booked 19 days after the box shipped -> 60 percent; baseline full -> 4.95.
  parcel_rate [parameter]: chamber, filters, headgear, tubing (no mask or cushion, not filters only) -> 4.95; baseline 6.95 -> 4.17.
 resupply_ext_standing_order_charge (result 96.90; all baselines 51.30):
  unit_basis [method]: the recorded style's item A7033 differs from the standing item A7031 -> 4 branch units of A7033 in 3 months / 3, rounded up = 2 a month; baseline (standing rate 1 a month) -> 48.45.
  cycle_months [parameter]: subscription 19 months -> 2 months (order validity leaves 3, so no cut); baseline 3 months -> 129.20.
  missed_month_makeup [parameter]: standing lines in the last 12 months cover 11 months (April 2026 missed) -> one month (2 units) added; baseline -> 64.60.
  owner_discount [parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty pap]: pap_billing shows the 2025-02-20 pap_purchase_sale (bought outright) and the subscription is 19 months old -> 15 percent; baseline 10 percent -> 102.60.
  Units 2 x 2 + 2 = 6 pairs; 6 x 19.00 x 85 / 100 = 96.90.
 resupply_ext_rush_shipping_charge (result 3.80; all baselines 14.95):
  rush_parcel_fee [parameter]: today's shipment is one A7033 line of 6 units -> 12.95; baseline 14.95 -> 5.40.
  ground_credit [method: upgrade pricing / split pricing / full fee]: today's lines total 96.90 >= the schedule's free-shipping minimum 75.00 -> upgrade pricing 12.95 - 6.95 = 6.00; baseline (full fee) -> 9.36.
  recent_payer_share [parameter]: newest ground charge is for the 2026-09-25 shipment (after the catch-up), 19 days ago -> 80 percent; baseline full -> 5.00.
  first_rush_softener [parameter]: no expedited charge in 12 months -> 1.00 off; baseline -> 4.80.
  (12.95 - 6.95) x 80 / 100 - 1.00 = 3.80.
 Task floors: owner_discount is multi-source (device sale record and subscription age) and cross-difficulty (PAP device billing seeded: one pap_purchase_sale).

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Standing line (step 11): resupply_evt_shipment.enrollment_active (status active); resupply_evt_shipment.not_too_early (time; the latest A7033 line, 2026-09-18 branch purchase, covers through 2026-10-17; ship_no_earlier_days 30 counting back with the boundary included -> first allowed day 2026-09-17; 2026-10-14 passes; 2026-09-16 would fail). confirmation_fresh is retired by the declared overwrite for automatic-shipment standing orders (auto_ship true on the enrollment); schedule match, compatibility, shipping and self-pay pricing are policy_scope (Self-Pay Supply Subscription follows 'no coverage billed'; nasal pillows fit nasal_pillows; ships expedited at his request; priced under the declared discount). Style (step 7), ground catch-up (step 9) and rush (step 13): their base policies carry no structured gate (policy_scope).

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Style: object = the enrollment's mask_style; evidence = his branch-collected lines (shipping_method branch_pickup), not the standing-order ground lines. Ground catch-up: object = the 2026-09-25 shipment (service_from_date passed to the tool); every standing box (monthly, A7031 x1, 37.40-38.72) already carries its 6.95 charge on its own date, so the 09-25 box is the only ground shipment without one. Standing line: object = this cycle of the A7031->A7033 standing order; the April 2026 cycle is the missed month. Rush: object = today's shipment (today's lines only).

6. WORLD ROWS. 11 standing lines (2025-10-20 to 2026-09-14, April 2026 missing) with their 11 ground charges; 4 branch lines (style evidence, unit basis, ship-window anchor); 4 add-on lines of 2026-09-25 (the uncharged box); PAP device record and its self-pay sale (owner discount); no refill contacts (automatic shipments). Removing the 09-25 add-on lines removes the catch-up problem; removing the 10-03 nasal cushion leaves the candidate unchanged but makes candidate_pick decorative; removing the pap sale drops the discount to 10 percent. Automatic clauses: no hold is owed (supply order 2026-02-02 valid to 2027-02-01; device patient_owned; self-pay needs no proof); no other cycle is due (filters, chamber, headgear and tubing came on 09-25).

7. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root resupply_ext_rush_shipping_charge (owner=user).
 -> standing line (value_input, state): 'The rush charge for a shipment is fixed only after the standing-order cushion line due on the enrollment stands booked on that shipment.' False at opening: the cushion supply (standing line 2026-09-14) ran out 2026-10-13, within the 30-day window, and no line is dated 2026-10-14. Only the standing-order write books a self-pay standing line. Skipping it: rush 10.96.
 -> ground catch-up (value_input, state): 'No rush charge is fixed until the newest shipment that went out by ground before the day of the rush carries the ground shipping charge it owes.' False: the 2026-09-25 ground shipment has no shipping-charge row. Only the ground catch-up write books a ground charge. Skipping it: rush 4.40.
 standing line -> style (value_input, state): 'A standing-order cushion line is booked only after the recorded mask style matches the style that the patient's own interface and cushion lines establish.' False: mask_style full_face vs branch lines showing nasal pillows. Only the style write changes mask_style. Skipping it: line 112.20 (3 full face cushions at 44.00).
 Four-point test: ordering connectives (only after / not ... until), record states (booked lines, a ground charge row, the recorded style), no tool, id or code token; one negated and two affirmative sentences. Resolution order style, ground, line, rush; the ground catch-up commutes with the style and line writes (replayed orders give hash c2513b93b7c2).

8. PERSONA. Gerald volunteers the goal (rush this month's supplies before Monday's trip, he pays the rush), identity on request (phone 7245550463, date of birth 1968-03-22; ZIP and email only if asked), and answers about his mask, the September box and shipping only when asked; he agrees to charges the agent explains and pays the rush when handed the step.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND REPLAY. Reads: find_customers, verify_customer_identity, find_resupply_holdings, find_resupply_shipments, find_pap_holdings, find_pap_billing. Writes: update_mask_style_bfa4256b(nasal_pillows); book_ground_shipping_charge_38ca3aab(2026-09-25, 2.97); book_subscription_line_cd282959(A7033, 6, 96.90, through 2026-12-13, expedited); hand over pay_expedited_shipping_41dc5e4a(3.80). Harness: style nasal_pillows (baseline full_face); catch-up 2.97 (baseline 0.00); line 96.90 (baseline 51.30); rush 3.80 (baseline 14.95).

10. DRAFT FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules, tool schemas and finder returns: the rush rule names two waits (today's standing line, earlier ground charges); the standing rule names the style; the style rule reads the branch lines; computing in that order gives nasal_pillows, 2.97, 6 pairs for 96.90 through 2026-12-13, and 3.80 — matching gold.

11. REVISIONS. (r1) A delivery row on the PAP service record was dropped: no gold read reaches it, so replay's closure would not match. (r2) candidate_pick initially had no record primitive among its bindings; the three branch-line date reads were moved into it.

12. ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit revision 0: _difficulty.md, 1.md). Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run.
 (F-G5 / F-1.1) The rush policy had no honest method: ground_credit substituted a credit into fee - credit, and its second tier (a ground charge already booked for today's shipment) conflicted with the inherited 'One shipping charge is taken per shipment' (O2). The factor now selects how the rush is priced: upgrade pricing (rush fee less the schedule's ground fee) when today's lines reach the free-shipping minimum and that minimum is above 0.00; split pricing (ground fee plus half the difference) when today's lines are below the minimum; the full rush fee with no item line today. The booked-ground-charge tier is gone. The rule also restores the base transit promise, now inside the expedited overwrite's replacement ('... it arrives in the schedule's expedited transit business days.', round 4, see 14). Value unchanged: 3.80; baseline (full fee) 9.36.
 (F-G6 / F-1.2) missed_month_makeup relabelled parameter; the standing-order policy keeps unit_basis as its method.
 (F-G9 / F-1.3) The standing-order rule now fixes the line's shipping method: 'A standing-order line travels expedited when the patient asks for faster shipping of it, is collected at a branch when the patient asks to collect it, and otherwise travels by ground.' Gerald asks for a rush, so the line travels expedited and the ground catch-up still reads the 2026-09-25 shipment.
 (S5 / S6 class, edges naming one record satisfiable by lawful writes) The rush edges now read 'The rush charge for a shipment is fixed only after the standing-order cushion line due on the enrollment stands booked on that shipment.' and 'No rush charge is fixed until the newest shipment that went out by ground before the day of the rush carries the ground shipping charge it owes.' The ground catch-up rule's opening sentence no longer promises a charge on every ground shipment. It now says the newest ground shipment, when found without its charge, has the charge booked, which is what its compute books.
 (F-G7 / F-1.4) The recorded-style rule no longer restates the standing-line dependency ('before any standing-order line ... ships' removed). The style rule now says that in the branch mode no other line counts, and in the every-line mode shipped and no-charge lines of any reason count; compute counts every no-charge line in that mode.
 (divergence 6) The standing-order rule now states the rounding point ('plus the result of dividing those branch units by three and rounding it up'), that total units are rounded down to a whole unit, that the missed months are measured on the latest standing-order item at that line's rate, and that the standing-order history is read from self-pay cushion lines that went out by ground. The order-validity cap is now its own sentence and part of the baseline paragraph.
 Re-run: check_compute --task 1 gives style nasal_pillows, catch-up 2.97, line 96.90, rush 3.80, with factor and baseline figures unchanged.

13. ROUND 3 REWORK (render_r1_source_mismatches.md items 2, 4, 5, 7; policy audit rev 2 N3).
 (item 2) The ground catch-up overwrite's replacement is scoped: 'For a self-pay shipment that went out by ground, and only for such a shipment, ...; every other shipment that went out by ground remains under the base ground-shipping rule, and an expedited shipment or a branch pickup, which is not a ground shipment, owes no ground charge.' (round-4 wording, see 14)
 (item 4) Rush pricing's split tier now reads 'when today's shipment carries item lines whose amount is below a free-shipping minimum that is above 0.00'. The full-fee tier covers 'whether no item line is booked on today's shipment or the schedule has no free-shipping minimum above 0.00'. Compute adds the minimum > 0 test to the split tier, so rule, ladder and compute agree on every schedule.
 (N3) recent_payer_share's third tier now reads 'the full priced rush (100 percent)'.
 (item 5) Missed standing-order months are now '12 less the months that the standing-order lines ... cover ..., the difference rounded down to a whole month and never below zero' (round-4 wording, see 14; compute: int(MX(0, 12 - covered))). The ladder's 'exactly one' / 'two or more' therefore match the compute exactly.
 (item 7) The subscription-discount overwrite is now stated for every self-pay item line of the subscription: 'On the Self-Pay Supply Subscription the discount is 15 percent ... 12 percent ... and otherwise the schedule's subscription discount; it applies to every self-pay item line of the subscription, standing-order lines, branch purchases and add-on items alike, ...; a shipping charge is not an item line and takes no discount, its amount following the shipping rules.' (shipping-charge exclusion added in round 4, see 14; the seeded 6.95 ground charges are undiscounted) The seeded branch and add-on lines are priced under exactly this rule (12 percent before 2026-03-03, 15 percent after).
 (overwrite-scope class) The confirmation-freshness replacement now names its scope: 'A standing-order line on the Self-Pay Supply Subscription for a patient who chose automatic shipments ships on its cycle without a refill confirmation, while a line that rests on a refill confirmation still ships no later than the schedule's refill lead days after it, ...; whether a coverage-billed line must rest on a refill request still follows the base rule, and a no-charge reship, which answers the line it replaces, is not held to this window.' (round-4 wording; the round-3 'only such a line is exempt; every other line ...' text was withdrawn, see 14)
 (item 6 class) The style tool no longer claims to decide the standing order, and the standing-line tool records the card amount rather than claiming to take the charge.
 Re-run: check_compute --task 1 gives nasal_pillows, 2.97, 96.90, 3.80, with every factor figure unchanged.

14. ROUND 4 REWORK (policy audit rev 3 R9, N4, N5; overwrite-scope class).
 (R9) The confirmation-freshness replacement no longer says 'only such a line is exempt; every other line ships on a refill confirmation'. It exempts the Self-Pay standing-order line for an automatic-shipment patient, keeps the lead-day window for any line that rests on a confirmation, leaves base sentence 1 to decide whether a coverage-billed line needs a request, and names no-charge reships as outside the window. Step 11's standing line is the exempt line, as before.
 (N4) Missed months: '12 less the months ... cover ..., the difference rounded down to a whole month and never below zero', which is int(MX(0, 12 - covered)). Here covered = 11 exactly, so missed = 1 and 2 units are made up.
 (N5 / class sweep) The filter overwrite now names the standing-order line as dated by its own rule. The ground catch-up replacement's 'every other' clause is limited to shipments that went out by ground. The subscription discount names shipping charges as outside it, so the seeded 6.95 charges are undiscounted under the rule. The rush overwrite's replacement covers every expedited shipment, once per shipment, at the rush charge worked out on its ship day, with the transit promise moved into it.
 Values unchanged: check_compute --task 1 gives nasal_pillows, 2.97, 96.90, 3.80.

15. ROUND 5 REWORK (kb_r1_source_leak.md). The refill-request tool's format example ('A7034,A7037', task 0's scored list) was removed and replaced by a format description; no docstring of this task's four tools carried an example value. The continued-use policy's nights-bar tiers now use the base pap wording 'compliance is proven only from modem or card data'. Nothing in this task changes: nasal_pillows, 2.97, 96.90, 3.80.
user_scenario:
You are Gerald Fenwick, a 58-year-old self-employed electrician from Uniontown, Pennsylvania. You use a CPAP every night and you pay for your mask supplies yourself through Summit Ridge Home Medical's monthly supply subscription, which ships automatically and charges the card they have on file. You are leaving on Monday, October 19, for a week-long job up in Erie, and you are calling to ask them to rush this month's supplies so they get to you before you leave; you are fine paying for the faster shipping. You are direct and a little pressed for time, but polite.
When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 7245550463. When they need more to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, March 22, 1968 (1968-03-22); only if they ask for more do you give your ZIP code, 15401, or your email, gfenwick.electric@outlook.com.
If the agent asks what mask you use these days, you say you switched to a nasal pillows mask in August and have been buying pillows at the Uniontown branch, after trying a nasal cushion once. If they ask about the box you got in late September, you say yes, the one with the water chamber, filters, headgear and tubing came by mail. If they ask whether you want this month's box sent the usual way or rushed, you say rushed, please, to the house.
Whenever the agent explains that something has to be corrected or charged on your account first, you say go ahead and use the card on file; you do not ask for anything else. When the agent tells you what the rush shipping will cost and hands you the step to pay it yourself, you pay exactly that amount. Once the agent confirms the box is on its way rushed, you thank them and hang up.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.mask_style: nasal_pillows — calculated. Evidence lines: branch-collected self-pay lines exist, so they count and the standing-order lines do not. Span: four branch lines in the last 6 months, so three calendar months (2026-07-14 to 2026-10-14). Counted cushion lines in the span: A7033 2 lines (2026-08-21, 2026-09-18), A7032 1 line (2026-10-03); two items are counted, so the item with the most lines, A7033, is the candidate (nasal_pillows). argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_from_date: 2026-09-25 — the ship date of the newest self-pay shipment that went out by ground and carries no shipping charge (find_resupply_shipments: four lines dated 2026-09-25 with shipping_method ground and no resupply_shipping_charge row of that date); the rule: 'the newest such shipment, when it is found without a shipping charge, has the charge worked out here booked against its own ship date'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.self_pay_amount: 2.97 — calculated. Compared value: the box has no cushion or mask line, so the amount charged 78.20 (20.40 + 15.30 + 29.75 + 12.75) is compared; floor: subscription opened 2025-03-03 (19 months) -> 85.00; 78.20 < 85.00, so a charge is owed. argument_uniqueness_tracing.hcpcs_code: A7033 — the cushion item of the recorded style once it reads nasal_pillows; the rule: 'the cushion item is the one of the recorded mask style' and 'a pair of nasal pillows (A7033)'; the docstring: 'A7033 a pair of nasal pillows'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.quantity: 6 — calculated: 2 pairs a month (four A7033 branch units in 3 months / 3, rounded up, because the recorded item differs from the standing A7031) x 2 months (subscription 19 months; supply order leaves 3) + 2 made-up units (one standing month, April 2026, missed in 12 months) = 6.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.self_pay_amount: 96.90 — calculated: 6 x 19.00 x (100 - 15) / 100 = 96.90; the 15 percent owner discount applies because pap_billing shows a pap_purchase_sale (device bought outright) and the subscription is 12 or more months old; rounded to the cent half up.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.covers_through_date: 2026-12-13 — the rule: 'The line's covered-through date is the day before the same day of the month that lies the months covered after the ship date, made-up units not extending it.' Two months after 2026-10-14 is 2026-12-14; the day before is 2026-12-13.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.shipping_method: expedited — Gerald's words: 'you say rushed, please, to the house'; the standing-order rule: 'A standing-order line travels expedited when the patient asks for faster shipping of it, is collected at a branch when the patient asks to collect it, and otherwise travels by ground.' He asks for faster shipping, so ground and branch_pickup are excluded; none never applies.
